clue.text: See you, more than once, during overture to Ernani

indicators.note: said more than once, the three letters built from the rest of the clue are given a second time

parts.note: by can mean during, as in 'by night'

indicators.note: an overture opens a work, so the opening letter of Ernani is wanted

explanation.surface: An operagoer keeps saying farewell just as the prelude to Verdi's Ernani starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'More than once' tells you to repeat what 'during' and the opening of Ernani give, so the short farewell appears twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled farewell is a casual, rather childlike way of saying goodbye, the same parting as 'see you'.

clue.text: Tough young people mostly absorbing books

indicators.note: the shortened word takes the next piece into its middle
most of the word is kept, dropping its last letter

parts.note: yoof is a jokey spelling of youth, meaning young people collectively
B is the abbreviation for book, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Hardened youngsters are reluctantly taking in some reading.
explanation.walkthrough: YOOF, the slangy spelling of youth, loses its F to give YOO, which then takes in BB.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough here is a noun for a thuggish lout, which is what the British slang word denotes.

clue.text: Pluck outside of pheasants, say, or other kinds of sport

indicators.note: the word for pluck goes around the next piece

parts.note: balls is slang for courage or nerve, i.e. pluck
pheasants are an example of game birds

explanation.surface: A cook plucks the feathers off pheasants, or someone takes up some other pastime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pluck' reads as the verb for stripping feathers, but it is a noun for courage here.
explanation.definitionFit: Football, tennis, cricket and the like are sports played with a ball, hence these games.

clue.text: One expected to make final tried running round Oval?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the next piece
running in the sense of operating or working loose lets the letters of tried be rearranged

parts.note: an oval is the shape of the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone expected to reach a final has given it a go around a cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oval is a London cricket ground, which steers you to sport; here it simply gives the shape of O.
explanation.definitionFit: The person in charge of a publication gives copy its final form before printing.

clue.text: Go through the motions as issue backed on record

indicators.note: one piece is placed after the other

parts.note: to mark is to record, as in marking a score

indicators.note: backed means going in reverse, so the word for issue is read from its end

parts.note: to emit is to issue or send out

explanation.surface: Something is issued, then reversed, and it all goes on the record.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark time is to march on the spot, hence to do something without making real progress.

clue.text: Birds mass then cross into Western Sahara erratically

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for mass in physics

indicators.note: the cross is placed inside the rearranged letters
erratically means irregularly, so the letters of Western Sahara are jumbled

parts.note: X is the shape of a cross

explanation.surface: A great flock of birds strays across the desert of north-west Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of WESTERN SAHARA rearranged give ANSHEARWATERS, with X placed after the N.
explanation.definitionFit: The Manx shearwater is a seabird named after the Isle of Man, where it once bred in great numbers.

clue.text: Current regulator's letter from Greece intercepted by English immediately

indicators.note: the Greek letter has the next piece caught in its middle

parts.note: rho is the Greek letter R
stat is medical shorthand for immediately

explanation.surface: A message from Athens is seized by the English at once.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a variable resistor used to control the flow of electricity in a circuit.

clue.text: Fish stuck in waste trap

indicators.note: the answer is lodged within the run of letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A fish has got caught in a drain trap.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brightly coloured tropical freshwater species often kept in aquariums.

clue.text: Partial cover-ups of leg fine in short skirts

indicators.note: the two pieces go inside the word for short skirts

parts.note: minis are miniskirts
on is the leg side in cricket
OK means fine, all right

explanation.surface: Skimpy garments covering part of the leg are fine worn with miniskirts.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is also called the on side, so 'leg' gives ON.
explanation.definitionFit: These are topless swimsuits, bikini bottoms only, so they cover the body only partly.

clue.text: European papal edict that is pleasant without beginning to invite enthusiasm

parts.note: a bull is a formal decree issued by the Pope
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is taken out of the word for pleasant

parts.note: nice means pleasant

indicators.note: the beginning of the word invite is its first letter

explanation.surface: A pleasant papal decree from Europe is drawn up to stir up zeal.
explanation.walkthrough: NICE loses I, the first letter of 'invite', to give NCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means bubbling exuberance, a lively cheerfulness and energy.

clue.text: Insignificant short chap escaping unavoidable fate

indicators.note: the chap's name gets out of the word for fate, leaving the rest

parts.note: destiny is fate that cannot be avoided
Des is a short form of the man's name Desmond

explanation.surface: A small man manages to dodge his doom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like it describes the answer, but it belongs to the name: Des is short for Desmond.
explanation.definitionFit: Something very small is trivially minor, so of little importance.

clue.text: Magnificent valley moguls regularly visited

parts.note: a gorge is a narrow steep-sided valley

indicators.note: only every other letter of moguls is called on, at even steps

explanation.surface: Splendid ski bumps in the valley got frequent visits.
explanation.walkthrough: Moguls are the bumps on a ski slope, which suits the valley scene; take its 2nd, 4th and 6th letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something strikingly beautiful or splendid.

clue.text: Lively plonk quaffed by Sunday on vacation

indicators.note: the word for plonk is drunk into, so goes inside, the next letters
vacated, the word keeps only its outer letters

parts.note: Sunday emptied of its middle leaves its first and last letters
to plonk something down is to park it

explanation.surface: Cheap wine is drunk merrily by holidaymakers on a Sunday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plonk' is British slang for cheap wine, which suits 'quaffed'; here it is the verb to put down, so PARK.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone full of spark is spirited and animated, the British informal sense.

clue.text: Did fly perhaps gather with colony leaving river

definitions.note: past tense: fly is short for butterfly, a swimming stroke

indicators.note: the river's letter departs from the word for gathering

parts.note: bees swarm when they gather together as a colony on the move

explanation.surface: An insect wonders whether it gathered with its colony and left the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' looks like an insect, fitting the colony, but it is the butterfly stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing the butterfly is one example of moving through water by stroke, hence this past tense.

clue.text: Shy, retiring, getting husband demoted without deserving contempt

indicators.note: the letter for husband is moved lower, to the end
retiring means going back, so the word for shy is reversed

parts.note: to shy is to throw
less means without, as in 'a pound less tax'

explanation.surface: A timid, retiring woman's husband has been demoted, and she gets no contempt for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shy' looks like timid, matching 'retiring', but it is the verb meaning to throw; 'demoted' sends the husband's letter down to the bottom of the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of no value at all merits only scorn, so the adjective fits.

clue.text: Milking former luvviedom?

parts.note: ex means former
luvvies are actors, so luvviedom is the theatre world, the profession of acting

explanation.surface: A retired thespian is still squeezing everything from their old stage career.
explanation.walkthrough: Luvvie is British slang for an effusive actor.
explanation.definitionFit: To exact is to extort or squeeze out, as one does when one milks a person or situation.

clue.text: Conductor of opera concerned with repeated upset

parts.note: Tosca is Puccini's opera

indicators.note: repeated asks for the little word twice over, and upset, in a down answer, turns the pair bottom to top

parts.note: in means involved or concerned with, as in 'in shipping'; the clue wants it twice

explanation.surface: An opera conductor is concerned with an upsetting repeat performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Arturo Toscanini was a celebrated Italian maestro who led orchestras such as the NBC Symphony.

clue.text: Frank after service not on VAT radar?

indicators.note: the word for frank follows the one for service

parts.note: duty is service, as in on duty
frank means free, as in a franked letter sent without postage charge

explanation.surface: A man named Frank, finishing his service, wonders about value added tax.
explanation.walkthrough: VAT is the UK sales tax, value added tax; 'Frank' poses as a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods sold exempt from customs and tax charges escape the taxman's notice, so sit off the radar.

clue.text: Shorter fighter, not one grasping question

indicators.note: the shortened word holds the next piece in its middle
not tells you the numeral for one is dropped

parts.note: a bruiser is a tough fighter
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A boxer without an equal clutches at a question.
explanation.definitionFit: Shorter in the sense of more curt, a more abrupt manner of speaking.

clue.text: Framework made of, primarily, seasoned wood

indicators.note: primarily means first, so the opening letter of seasoned

parts.note: ash is a tree and its timber

explanation.surface: A frame is built first of all from well-seasoned timber.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is the framework holding the glass panes in a window.

clue.text: Go work in post office, collecting fines

indicators.note: the work is put inside the post office

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
F stands for fine (a pencil grade), doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: Someone goes off to take a job at the post office, where they collect payment of penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: To pop off is slang for to die, and go is a euphemism for dying.

clue.text: In Cyprus, hotel that's horrid and rude

indicators.note: the following pieces are placed inside Cyprus's code

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet
eek is the cry one gives at something horrid

explanation.surface: A hotel in Cyprus is described as awful and impolite.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent, disrespectful or impertinent behaviour is cheeky, the slightly playful sense of rude.

clue.text: Special edition, 50 per cent of 1, perhaps

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an additional issue of a newspaper published for breaking news
second meaning: half of 1-across is BYE, which in cricket is an example of a run not scored off the bat

explanation.walkthrough: Half of 1-across is BYE; in cricket a bye is one kind of run credited to the side without the batsman hitting the ball, all such runs being of this type.
explanation.definitionFit: Newspapers once printed an additional edition for big news, and cricket's sundries are runs not off the bat.

clue.text: Charming adult party with half-hearted chatter

parts.note: A is the film-classification abbreviation for adult
a do is a party

indicators.note: the double letters at the heart lose half, one of the pair

parts.note: to rabble is an old word meaning to gabble or chatter

explanation.surface: A grown-up's party is lovely despite the lacklustre small talk.
explanation.walkthrough: RABBLE has BB at its heart; half-hearted removes one B to leave RABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe something delightful that inspires affection.

clue.text: Get rest around middle of afternoon

indicators.note: the word for rest goes around the next letter

parts.note: to lean is to rest on something

indicators.note: the central letter of afternoon

explanation.surface: Someone takes a mid-afternoon rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To get something, in the sense of to grasp or understand it, is to come to know it.

clue.text: Outwit what could follow all the next level

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to get the better of someone

definitions.text: what could follow all the next level
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the word completes 'all the ...', 'next ...' and 'level ...'

explanation.walkthrough: The second part is a list of three separate lead-ins, 'all the', 'next' and 'level', each completed by the same word; it is not a phrase about reaching a next level.
explanation.definitionFit: To get the better of someone in a contest is to defeat them.

clue.text: Unlimited short article reprinted and inflated

indicators.note: printed again, so the letters are reset in a new order
without its limits the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: the word itself used as letters

explanation.surface: A brief newspaper piece is reprinted, but bloated beyond all bounds.
explanation.walkthrough: SHORT without its limits gives HOR; add ARTICLE and rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Bombastic, overblown language is rhetorical, showy speech aimed at effect.

clue.text: Look back on space travelling — they're off!

indicators.note: one piece follows the other
travelling means moving around, so the letters of space are rearranged
the word for look is read from its end

parts.note: to see is to look

explanation.surface: Someone looks back on space travel as a race starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'They're off!' is a racing cry, but here it describes people who have got away.
explanation.definitionFit: These are people who have broken free from captivity and fled.

clue.text: Intimate relationship initially stifled by brute

indicators.note: the letter is smothered inside the word for brute

parts.note: a fiend is a cruel brute

indicators.note: the first letter of relationship

explanation.surface: A close relationship is stifled at the outset by a brutal partner.
explanation.definitionFit: An intimate, as a noun, is a close companion or confidant.
